editorial:
Imagine you are a writer who is totally stuck and lonely, and then suddenly, the perfect girl you wrote about in your notebook just appears on your couch. That is exactly what happens to Calvin in this quirky story. It starts off feeling like a fun fantasy where you get to design your dream partner, but it quickly turns into something much deeper. You get to see Calvin struggle with the fact that he can actually control Ruby's feelings and personality just by typing on his typewriter. It is a sweet and slightly weird look at how we try to change the people we love to fit our own needs.

Zoe Saldana is great as Ruby, and the way the movie balances the funny parts with the sad parts works really well. The pacing is smooth, though some people might find the ending a bit slow. If you like stories about love and magic, you will really enjoy this one. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the cozy details of the settings.
endingExplained: After trying to control Ruby for too long, Calvin realizes that loving someone means letting them be their own person. He decides to write one last sentence that gives Ruby her own free will. Once she is free, Ruby chooses to leave him because he was too controlling. They both grow from the experience, and the movie ends with them meeting again as equals, finally capable of having a real, healthy relationship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic stories with a supernatural twist.
